source_text:
Ἔδειξέ μοι πάλιν δένδρα πολλά, ἃ μὲν βλαστῶντα, ἃ δὲ ξηρά, καὶ λέγει μοι: Βλέπεις, φησί, τὰ δένδρα ταῦτα; Βλέπω, φημί, κύριε, τὰ μὲν βλαστῶντα τὰ δὲ ξηρά.
Ταῦτα, φησί, τὰ δένδρα τὰ βλαστῶντα οἱ δίκαιοί εἰσιν οἱ μέλλοντες κατοικεῖν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τὸν ἐρχόμενον: ὁ γὰρ αἰὼν ὁ ἐρχόμενος θερεία ἐστὶ τοῖς δικαίοις, τοῖς δὲ ἁμαρτωλοῖς χειμών. ὅταν οὖν ἐπιλάμψῃ τὸ ἔλεος τοῦ κυρίου, τότε φανερωθήσονται οἱ δουλεύοντες τῷ θεῷ, καὶ πάντες φανερωθήσονται.
ὥσπερ γὰρ τῷ θέρει ἑνὸς ἑκάστου δένδρου οἱ καρποὶ φανεροῦνται καὶ ἐπιγινώσκονται ποταποί εἰσιν, οὕτω καὶ τῶν δικαίων οἱ καρποὶ φανεροὶ ἔσονται καὶ γνωσθήσονται πάντες εὐθαλεῖς ὄντες ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι ἐκείνῳ.
τὰ δὲ ἔθνη καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοί, ἃ εἶδες τὰ δένδρα τὰ ξηρά, τοιοῦτοι εὑρεθήσονται ξηροὶ καὶ ἄκαρποι ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ αἰῶνι καὶ ὡς ξύλα κατακαυθήσονται καὶ φανεροὶ ἔσονται, ὅτι ἡ πρᾶξις αὐτῶν πονηρὰ γέγονεν ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτῶν. οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἁμαρτωλοὶ καυθήσονται, ὅτι ἥμαρτον καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν: τὰ δὲ ἔθνη καυθήσονται, ὅτι οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τὸν κτίσαντα αὐτούς.
σὺ οὖν καρποφόρησον, ἵνα ἐν τῷ θέρει ἐκείνῳ γνωσθῇ σου ὁ καρπός: ἀπέχου δὲ ἀπὸ πολλῶν πράξεων καὶ οὐδὲν διαμαρτήσεις. οἱ γὰρ τὰ πολλὰ πράσσοντες πολλὰ καὶ ἁμαρτάνουσι, περισπώμενοι περὶ τὰς πράξεις αὐτῶν καὶ μηδὲν δουλεύοντες τῷ κυρίῳ ἑαυτῶν.
πῶς οὖν, φησίν, ὁ τοιοῦτος δύναταί τι αἰτήσασθαι παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ λαβεῖν, μὴ δουλεύων τῷ κυρίῳ; οἱ δουλεύοντες αὐτῷ, ἐκεῖνοι λήψονται τὰ αἰτήματα αὐτῶν. οἱ δὲ μὴ δουλεύοντες τῷ κυρίῳ, ἐκεῖνοι οὐδὲν λήψονται.
ἐὰν δὲ μίαν τις πρᾶξιν ἐργάσηται, δυναται καὶ τῷ κυρίῳ δουλεῦσαι: οὐ γὰρ διαφθαρήσεται ἡ διάνοια αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου, ἀλλὰ δουλεύσει αὐτῷ ἔχων τὴν διάνοιαν αὐτοῦ καθαράν.
ταῦτα οὖν ἐὰν ποιήσῃς, δύνασαι καρποφορῆσαι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τὸν ἐρχόμενον: καὶ ὃς ἂν ταῦτα ποιήσῃ, καρποφορήσει.
thought_title: The fruit-bearing and the dry trees in the coming age
orientation: The Shepherd shows Hermas the trees again, some now budding and some dry. They picture the righteous and the sinners in the age to come.
pass_a_gloss: He showed me again many trees, some sprouting, but others dry, and he says to me: Do you see, he says, these trees? I see, I say, lord, some sprouting but others dry. These, he says, the sprouting trees are the righteous, the ones who are about to dwell in the coming age: for the coming age is summer to the righteous, but to the sinners winter. Whenever therefore the mercy of the Lord shines forth, then the ones serving God will be made manifest, and all will be made manifest. For just as in summer of each single tree the fruits are made manifest and are recognized of what sort they are, so also of the righteous the fruits will be manifest and all will be known, being flourishing in that age. But the nations and the sinners, which you saw the dry trees, such they will be found, dry and fruitless in that age, and as wood they will be burned up and will be manifest, because their deed has become evil in their life. For the sinners will be burned, because they sinned and did not repent: but the nations will be burned, because they did not know the one who created them. You therefore bear fruit, so that in that summer your fruit may be known: but keep away from many deeds and you will in nothing fail. For the ones doing many things also sin many things, being distracted about their deeds and serving nothing to their own Lord. How therefore, he says, can such a one ask anything from the Lord and receive, not serving the Lord? The ones serving him, those will receive their requests. But the ones not serving the Lord, those will receive nothing. But if someone works one deed, he is able also to serve the Lord: for his mind will not be corrupted away from the Lord, but he will serve him having his mind pure. These things therefore if you do, you are able to bear fruit into the coming age: and whoever does these things, will bear fruit.

choices.why: The Shepherd contrasts summer and winter as the condition of the coming age for the righteous and sinners; 'summer' preserves the seasonal metaphor of fruit-bearing and flourishing.
The passive form emphasizes that God's mercy reveals them; 'made manifest' keeps the passive force and the eschatological disclosure.
The adjective describes the righteous as thriving like healthy trees in the coming age; 'flourishing' captures the botanical image.
The imperative continues the tree metaphor; 'bear fruit' is the natural English for producing fruit as a tree does.
The participle explains why those doing many things sin: they are pulled away from serving the Lord by their many activities.

pass_b_english: The Shepherd showed me many trees again, some budding and some dry. He said to me, “Do you see these trees?” “I see them, sir,” I said. “Some are budding, and some are dry.”

“These trees that are budding,” he said, “are the righteous, who are going to live in the age to come. For the age to come is summer for the righteous, but winter for sinners. So when the mercy of the Lord shines out, then those who serve God will be plainly seen, and all will be plainly seen.

“In summer the fruits of each tree are plainly seen, and it is known what kind they are. In the same way the fruits of the righteous will be plain to see, and all of them will be known to be flourishing in that age.

“But the nations and the sinners are the dry trees you saw. That is how they will be found in that age, dry and fruitless. They will be burned up like firewood, and they will be plain to see, because their conduct during their life was evil. The sinners will be burned because they sinned and did not repent. The nations will be burned because they did not know the one who created them.

“As for you, bear fruit, so that in that summer your fruit may be known. Keep away from many business affairs, and you will not sin in anything. For those who do much business also sin much. They are distracted by their business affairs, and they do not serve their Lord at all.

“How, then,” he said, “can such a man ask anything of the Lord and receive it, when he does not serve the Lord? Those who serve him will receive what they ask. But those who do not serve the Lord will receive nothing.
“But if a man works at one business only, he can serve the Lord as well. For his mind will not be corrupted and drawn away from the Lord. He will serve him with a pure mind.
“So if you do these things, you can bear fruit for the age to come. And whoever does these things will bear fruit.”

checks.via: blind check of the tuned English, clean at round 0 (tune_check.py)

last_rejected.quote: and you will go astray in nothing
last_rejected.why: διαμαρτάνω means 'miss the mark, fail, err', not 'go astray' in sense of wander; better 'you will miss nothing' or 'you will not fail'
last_rejected.fix: and you will not fail in anything
last_rejected.ruling: διαμαρτάνω means 'err, fail, miss'; 'go astray in nothing' conveys not erring/failing. Within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: his mind will not be corrupted away from the Lord
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐ γὰρ διαφθαρήσεται ἡ διάνοια αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου
last_rejected.why: ἀπό here means separation/departure from, not 'away from' as corruption's source; 'diverted from' or 'drawn away from' the Lord
last_rejected.fix: For his mind will not be drawn away from the Lord
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπό with διαφθείρω denotes separation; 'corrupted away from the Lord' correctly renders departure from God. Acceptable rendering.
